content.thinking:
I'm laying out the postmortem: the symptom is that account pages failed for many shoppers, with errors seen in requests Gbac1 and G5309. The causal chain starts with those failed account page requests (Gbac1, G5309, AL1), and the next step is that the requests raised a ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summ.

I'm checking which changes landed before the errors began: the monthly-spend flag was switched on at P1 by an admin, and flag evaluations moved from off to on. I'm ruling out deploys, since the records show no production change in that window except the flag itself.

I'm checking whether any deploy could explain the onset, and I'm ruling it out: no deploy was read back in the day before the errors started, and all three replicas ran one revision, which the metrics show was healthy during the 361 minutes before onset.

I'm noting that the flag routes the account page figure through a per-item average, which divides by the number of purchases this month, so shoppers with no purchases this month hit a zero count. The line number in the trace matches that path, though the empty-list mechanism is only supported by the code reading so far.

I'm working out the contributing factors now: the flag was switched on without a test for shoppers with no purchases this month, and it went live for all traffic at once rather than in stages.

I'm listing the contributing factors now: the flag went from off to on for all requests within a single minute, with no staged rollout, which I'm treating as something to prevent with gradual rollouts that halt on rising errors. I'm also noting that nobody was paged during the incident, and I'm weighing whether that belongs under what went wrong rather than as a factor.

I'm deciding how to phrase the action items, starting with a pre-switch check that requires tests covering the code path a feature flag turns on, including shoppers with no purchases this month.

I'm adding the follow-up items: test the code path behind a flag, including empty-data cases, before it can be switched on in production, and roll out io-shop flags in stages, starting with a small share of requests, with a rollback if errors rise. I'm also noting that nobody was paged, so I'm proposing a page for the on-call person whenever HighErrorRate fires on io-shop.

I'm settling on how to say what could still go wrong: account pages could fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month if the monthly-spend flag is switched back on, and I'm leaving out the no-purchases error with the flag off, since the tests seem to expect it.

I'm settling on the lessons learned: the Investigator Agent tied the onset to the flag switch and named it as the one candidate, the Mitigation Agent reverted the flag and then confirmed the service was back within the incident's level, and the Code-Fix Agent proposed a draft fix with tests. The gap I'm noting is that nobody was paged during the incident.

I'm working out the root cause now: with the monthly-spend flag on, the account page's spend figure runs through the per-item average function in the spend summary module, and that is where the division by zero comes from.

I'm settling on the root cause: with the monthly-spend flag on, the account page's spend figure goes through a per-item average that divides this month's spend by the count of purchases made this month, so shoppers with no purchases this month hit a zero divisor and the request fails.

I'm checking the postmortem's wording, and I'm settling on how to say what the monthly-spend feature does: an administrator switched it on, and the code it turns on likely divides by zero for every shopper who has made no purchases this month. Account pages failed for many shoppers, and I'm tying that to the failing requests logged at G5309.

I'm drafting the ruled-out part of the chain now: the flag history shows no other flag change in the hour before the errors began, apart from the switch-on itself. That leaves the mechanism to check against the code path next.

I'm noting that the contributing factor being written up is the absence of any check before the flag went live, so I'm drafting how to phrase it without adding detail beyond what the postmortem records.

I'm drafting the contributing factor about the missing check, and I'm noting that the division by zero would have been caught before any shopper hit it. For the second factor, I'm writing that the flag went live for all account page traffic at once, so only a small share of shoppers would have reached the failing path if it had been staged. I'm also noting that the Mitigation Agent switched the flag back off, a change that can be reversed, and I'm starting on the Investigator's part of the went-well list.

I'm noting that the Investigator Agent formed its candidate C1, which ties the onset to the flag switch and doesn't involve any deploy.

action_items.item: Require tests covering the code path a feature flag turns on, including cases with no data such as a shopper with no purchases this month, to pass before that flag can be switched on in production.
Switch io-shop feature flags on in stages, starting with a small share of requests, instead of for all traffic at once.
Automatically halt a staged flag rollout on io-shop and turn the flag back off when the error rate rises during the rollout.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call incident so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed: the service logged a rise in account page errors and failed account page requests.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors were first logged in the onset minute and kept appearing until the logs read end.

ruled_out.what: A deployment: no deploy came back for the {T8.2} day {T8.3} minute before {T8.4}. All {T12.2} replicas ran a single revision, and the metrics read show the service healthy before the onset.
Any other flag change: the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus in the {T15.3} hour before {T15.4}, and that change is this switch-on.

causal_chain.step: The code path that raised the error was turned on when admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. In the service's own flag evaluations, every evaluation read off before the switch, the evaluations were split between off and on in the minute of the switch, and every evaluation read on after it.

With the flag on, the account page's spend figure goes through a function that divides by the number of purchases the shopper made this month. That number is zero for a shopper who has bought nothing this month, so the division fails.

input.cause_in_plain_words: An administrator switched on a new monthly-spending feature on the shop's account page, and the code it turned on then failed with a division by zero, likely for shoppers who had bought nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that ran the code path behind monthly-spend-feature for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before any shopper reached it, and the flag would not have been switched on while the fault was still there.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off to on for all account page traffic at once: evaluations were split only during the minute of the switch and were all on from the next minute. No staged rollout was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have reached the failing path before the rise in errors was caught and the flag turned back off.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent formed candidate C1, which tied the onset to the switch-on of monthly-spend-feature and to the ZeroDivisionError in the logs.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back off. This change can be put back.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed that the service was no longer at the incident's level after the revert.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix, with new tests, as draft pull request #547 for a person to review.

went_wrong: No on-call person was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page works out its spend figure in `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought nothing this month that number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and the request fails.
input.still_at_risk: Account pages could fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month if monthly-spend-feature is switched back on.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
